turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics

**What the training set says works in p‑i‑n MAPbI₃:**

1. **Hole contact quality dominates.** The best rows are almost all either (a) **PTAA** (deep, well‑matched HOMO ≈ –5.2 eV, non‑acidic, no ion‑extraction like PEDOT:PSS) → 17.2–19.1 %, or (b) **doped/passivated NiO‑c/NiO‑np** (Au‑np 20.0, SDBS 19.04, [BMIM]BF₄ 21.3, choline‑Cl 19.7). Plain PEDOT:PSS saturates around 13–16 % because its shallow work function (~5.0 eV) caps V_OC and its acidity degrades the buried interface. Au‑nanoparticle‑modified NiO is the single best HTL motif in the training set (20.0 %) — plasmonic/percolation‑enhanced hole extraction plus reduced series resistance.
2. **Fullerene + wide‑gap buffer + low‑work‑function‑free metal.** C60/PCBM capped with BCP/Bphen and finished with **Cu** (or Al with a polymer buffer) beats bare Ag in the training data (C60|BCP/PTAA/Cu = 18.6–19.1 % vs Ag = 17.2 %), because Cu gives an ohmic, non‑iodide‑reactive contact and BCP kills the fullerene/metal recombination dipole.
3. **Non‑fullerene / additional acceptor pre‑layers at the perovskite/ETL interface** (ITCPTC‑Th, NDP‑V, IDTT‑type PDIs, choline chloride, TTC) consistently raise the baseline by 1–2 % absolute by passivating under‑coordinated Pb and grading the electron cascade (ITCPTC‑Th|C60|BCP/P3CT‑Na = 18.49; PCBM|Bphen/PTAA|PMMA = 19.48).
4. **Substrate:** rigid SLG|ITO/FTO outperforms PET/PEN/textile/Ag‑nw substrates (rougher, more shunts, lower T).

**Applying this to the pool:**

- **c038** — PCBM‑60|PEI / **Au‑np | NiO‑c** / Ag: the top‑performing HTL architecture in training (20.0 %), plus a PEI dipole layer that lowers the ETL work function and improves electron selectivity. Best expected.
- **c030** — IDTT2FPDI | PCBM‑60 | Bphen / **PTAA | PMMA** / Al: exact analogue of the 19.48 % training row, with an extra non‑fullerene PDI passivation layer at the perovskite/ETL interface → highest V_OC potential.
- **c097** — ITCPTC‑Se | C60 | BCP / **P3CT‑Na** / Ag: direct Se‑analogue of the 18.49 % ITCPTC‑Th device; Se substitution deepens/broadens absorption and improves LUMO offset; P3CT‑Na is a high‑WF, non‑acidic polyelectrolyte HTL.
- **c044** — PCBM‑60|BCP / **PTAA** / **Cu**: the clean, proven PTAA + Cu combination (18.6–18.9 % family in training).
- **c085** — TTC | C60 | BCP / **PTAA** / Ag: silane/alkyl passivation layer on top of the PTAA‑grown perovskite baseline (17.2 %), a reliable +1 % interface‑passivation boost.

Close runners‑up (just outside): c088 (same PTAA/Cu chemistry but doctor‑bladed on willow glass), c041/c065 (Li,Mg‑doped NiO), c079 (NiO‑c|SY1), c095 (plasmonic NiO‑c).

**Final: c038, c030, c097, c044, c085**
